title: "svelte/no-immutable-reactive-statements"
description: "Disallow reactive statements that don't reference reactive values"
# Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit below this line.

A `$:` statement runs again when a value that it reads changes. When all it reads are constants, imports, functions or variables that are never assigned, it runs once and never again, so a plain statement says the same. Props (`export let`), stores (`$name`) and values that `bind:` or an `{#each}` over them can change count as reactive. The rule looks at components that are not in runes mode.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-immutable-reactive-statements": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<script>
  const price = 10;
  $: total = price * 2;
</script>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<script>
  export let price;
  $: total = price * 2;
</script>
```
